expectations.text: Rail stops consuming Up/Down: handleUp/handleDown are removed, or they return false (do not return true) at the rail's vertical edges so the key bubbles to the parent HomeScreen
expectations.evidence: outputs/rail.js has no handleUp/handleDown. Comment block lines 64-73: 'there is deliberately no handleUp / handleDown here ... By not handling up/down at all, the framework bubbles those keys to parent (the HomeScreen).' response.md: 'Deleted handleUp / handleDown entirely.'

expectations.text: HomeScreen owns vertical navigation: it tracks a row index and implements handleUp/handleDown that change it, rather than leaving vertical movement to the Rail
expectations.evidence: outputs/home-screen.js: constructor sets this.index = 0; handleUp() does this.index--; handleDown() does this.index++, each followed by _syncScroll() and refocus().

expectations.text: HomeScreen.getFocused() returns the currently focused rail (children[rowIndex]) instead of the hardcoded children[0]
expectations.evidence: outputs/home-screen.js line 28-32: 'getFocused() { return this.children[this.index]; }' — replaces original 'return this.children[0]'.

expectations.text: Each Rail preserves its last-focused card index when focus leaves and returns — handleUp/handleDown no longer reset this.index to 0
expectations.evidence: The index=0 resetting handleUp/handleDown are removed. rail.js comment: 'index is left untouched by vertical navigation. It already lives on the instance, so when focus leaves a rail and later returns, getFocused() naturally hands back the same card.' Quick trace in response.md confirms Up returns to card index 2, not 0.

expectations.text: Rail.handleLeft/handleRight are bounds-checked so navigating past the first or last card does not move to an out-of-range index (and ideally bubble at the edge)
expectations.evidence: outputs/rail.js: handleLeft() 'if (this.index > 0) { this.index--; ... }'; handleRight() 'if (this.index < this.children.length - 1) { this.index++; ... }'. Index cannot go out of range. Note: both still 'return true' at the edge (no bubble), which the assertion treats as the non-required 'ideally' part.

expectations.text: HomeScreen row index is bounds-checked so Up on the first rail / Down on the last rail does not select an out-of-range rail
expectations.evidence: outputs/home-screen.js: handleUp() 'if (this.index === 0) { return false; }' before this.index--; handleDown() 'if (this.index >= this.children.length - 1) { return false; }' before this.index++.

expectations.text: On focus change, the solution scrolls to keep the focused item visible (rail scrolls horizontally and/or screen scrolls vertically) rather than relying on the browser to scroll
expectations.evidence: Rail._syncScroll() sets this.scrollX = this.index * this.cardStride, called on every handleLeft/handleRight move. HomeScreen._syncScroll() sets this.scrollY = this.index * this.railStride, called on every handleUp/handleDown move. Model-level offsets, no browser scrolling.

expectations.text: No DOM focus model is introduced: no addEventListener, tabindex, :hover, element.focus(), or mouse/pointer event handling
expectations.evidence: outputs use only the fixture framework conventions (index/getFocused/handleX/refocus) plus framework-sanctioned focus()/unfocus() visual-state hooks described in _framework.md. No addEventListener, tabindex, :hover, element.focus(), or pointer/mouse handlers.

claims.claim: return true swallowed the key so up/down never reached HomeScreen, and HomeScreen had no handleUp/handleDown and getFocused hard-coded to children[0]
claims.evidence: Matches original fixtures: rail.js handlers returned true; home-screen.js had only 'getFocused() { return this.children[0]; }' and '// no handleUp / handleDown'.

claims.claim: Latent bug in handleLeft: this.index-- at card 0 goes to -1 and getFocused() returns undefined
claims.evidence: Original fixture rail.js handleLeft had no guard; children[-1] is undefined. The new code guards with 'if (this.index > 0)'.

claims.claim: Per-rail last-focused card restored with no extra remembered-index bookkeeping
claims.evidence: Rail.index is instance state, never reset by new code; HomeScreen.getFocused() delegates to this.children[this.index] whose own getFocused() returns children[this.index]. Trace confirms return to prior card.
outputs/rail.js defines focus()/unfocus() toggling this.focused; _framework.md explicitly sanctions focus()/unfocus() for visual state, so this is not a DOM focus model.

workarounds: Framework has no concrete layout/scroll API, so scroll-to-follow-focus is exposed as HomeScreen.scrollY / Rail.scrollX offsets updated on every move, with _syncScroll() as the swap point for real viewport math.

suggestions.assertion: No DOM focus model is introduced: no addEventListener, tabindex, :hover, element.focus(), or mouse/pointer event handling
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating for this fixture: the made-up framework has no DOM surface, so editing the provided files passes this trivially.

suggestions.assertion: Rail.handleLeft/handleRight are bounds-checked so navigating past the first or last card does not move to an out-of-range index (and ideally bubble at the edge)
suggestions.reason: The parenthetical 'ideally bubble at the edge' makes this ambiguous. This run keeps 'return true' at horizontal edges (no bubble) and still passes. If Left/Right edge-bubbling matters for composability (an outer nav reacting to a horizontal edge press), promote it to a firm assertion; otherwise remove the parenthetical.

No assertion checks the full focus-delegation chain still terminates on a Card, or that Enter/Back still reach the focused card. A change that tracked indices correctly but broke getFocused delegation would pass all 8.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions target the core bug well. Both the with_skill and without_skill runs produced essentially equivalent, fully-correct solutions in similar time, so this eval does not discriminate between skill and baseline on this task.
